kits.name: cloud-posture-review
kits.description: Two roles, one pipeline and one skill for read-only cloud posture and IAM review, where a check that could not run is NOT-CHECKED with its reason rather than a PASS.

skills.name: exposure-check
skills.line: Will not conclude "not exposed": the verdict names the checks that ran, their regions and the principal, and every denied API call is listed as a denial rather than a negative.

kits.name: complexity-guard
kits.description: Three roles, one pipeline and one skill for growth-rate review and measurement-disciplined optimization, where the role that states the number is never the role that wrote the code.

skills.name: scaling-check
skills.line: Names a growth class only when the measured ratios exclude every other one; otherwise reports not separable, the admitted classes and the deciding size.

kits.name: design-docs
kits.description: Four commands for the writing a repository asks for before code — an ADR, an architecture map, a fitness function and a high-level design — each refusing to assert what the tree does not show.

skills.name: adr-record
skills.line: Record one architecture decision as Proposed, with rejected alternatives only where the author supplied them or the repo shows they were tried.

skills.name: arch-map
skills.line: Map a codebase from resolved imports at file:line — no node and no edge without ledger evidence, and every unresolvable wiring listed rather than drawn.

skills.name: fitness-function
skills.line: Turn an architectural rule into a check and prove it bites — FAIL on a planted violation, PASS on HEAD, both transcripts, or the output is UNPROVEN CHECK.

skills.name: hld-draft
skills.line: Draft a high-level design as a scaffold with labelled holes — every constraint cited to a file:line or a quoted brief, everything else Assumed — unconfirmed.

kits.name: design-review-org
kits.description: Five roles and two pipelines that review a design before the code exists, where the document's author holds no shell and the human gate is a pause the engine enforces mid-pipeline.

kits.name: enterprise-org
kits.description: Eleven agent roles and six pipelines that carry a change from charter to merge gate, with the reviewers on lanes that structurally cannot land a patch.

kits.name: failure-design
kits.description: What happens when a dependency answers slowly. Retry safety is decided by an oracle that runs the operation twice — including the timeout case where the first attempt already committed — never by a reading.

skills.name: consistency-check
skills.line: Find dual writes, transaction boundaries that end earlier than the code assumes, and read-after-write races the storage does not guarantee.

skills.name: failure-modes
skills.line: Work every dependency through down, slow, wrong and partial, saying what actually happens at a path:line rather than that it is handled.

skills.name: retry-audit
skills.line: Find every retry, multiply the attempts across all layers, and report whether the operation underneath is safe to run twice.

skills.name: timeout-budget
skills.line: Trace the timeout chain hop by hop and find where it is absent, inverted, unbudgeted, or starving a shared pool.

kits.name: iac-plan-review
kits.description: One role, one pipeline and two skills for infrastructure change review that refuses to review a plan it did not produce, and treats the plan itself as code execution because on this domain's facts it is.

skills.name: plan-explain
skills.line: Explains a plan from the plan file alone, every sentence carrying a verbatim resource address; a resource it cannot classify as stateful is unknown, never assumed stateless, and it never concludes safe or no downtime.

skills.name: drift-report
skills.line: Attributes drift only to a quoted audit-log record with an event id, time and principal; everything else is unattributed. It proposes no state surgery and reads exit code 1 as an error, never as no drift.

kits.name: mobile-foundation
kits.description: Stand a mobile project up and keep it honest: toolchain from real doctor output, an architecture baseline proposed against the tree that exists, and an accessibility audit that runs what is runnable and names what it did not establish.

skills.name: a11y-sweep
skills.line: Audit mobile accessibility by running the checks this stack has and naming what source cannot decide. Emits no score and no conformance verdict.

skills.name: arch-baseline
skills.line: Map the architecture this repository actually has, then propose a baseline against it with the cost of each proposal named.

skills.name: env-doctor
skills.line: Report whether this machine can build this repository, from real commands with real exit codes, against the versions the repo pins.

skills.name: release-gate
skills.line: Check what a store will actually reject, from the manifests in this tree, never asserting that a build is signed, compliant or ready.

kits.name: mobile-ground-truth
kits.description: Four mobile commands that answer from the tree and the toolchain rather than from memory: API availability, crash triage, upgrade impact, privacy declarations.

skills.name: api-check
skills.line: Answer whether an API exists in the SDK you build against and whether it runs on the oldest OS you ship to, from files on this machine, never from memory.

skills.name: crash-triage
skills.line: Triage a mobile crash only when the trace is symbolicated and its symbols proven to match the shipped build; otherwise name what is missing and stop.

skills.name: privacy-declarations
skills.line: Draft the privacy-manifest and data-safety inputs a store asks for from what the code evidences, marking everything unevidenced as undeclarable.

skills.name: upgrade-impact
skills.line: Report only the breaking changes in an upgrade that actually occur in this repository, with the compiler's own deprecation output as the evidence.

kits.name: plan-pressure-tests
kits.description: Four reader skills that pressure-test a plan somebody already wrote — its assumptions, its feasibility against your tree, its claims and its cut order — each refusing the judgment it cannot ground.

skills.name: assumption-audit
skills.line: Grade the assumptions a plan rests on — SUPPORTED only with a file:line, a command's real output, or a page fetched this session; everything else is UNTESTED.

skills.name: feasibility-read
skills.line: Read a plan against this repository — what the tree supports at file:line, what searches came back empty with their patterns, and the unknowns. No estimate.

skills.name: rfc-review
skills.line: Review a design document for the comments that would change it — CONTRADICTED needs a file:line, HOLDS never rests on the document, and every drop is counted.

skills.name: scope-cut
skills.line: Order scope cuts by dependency read out of the import graph, every edge with its file:line — never by value, and no cut called safe without a named consumer.

kits.name: project-setup
kits.description: Stand a new app up with the ecosystem's own generator rather than files written from memory, then add the layering a generator leaves out — and prove the boundary check fails when the rule is broken.

skills.name: architecture-apply
skills.line: Add the layering a generator leaves out — boundaries, a composition root, a real test — on top of the tree that actually exists.

skills.name: boundary-prove
skills.line: Prove an architecture check fails when the rule is broken, by planting a violation and running it. BITES, TOOTHLESS or NO-ORACLE.

skills.name: scaffold-run
skills.line: Stand a project up with the ecosystem's own generator and report what actually landed. Never hand-writes a file a generator produces.

skills.name: stack-choose
skills.line: Choose a stack against a brief and this machine, with what every choice costs named. Takes acronyms like MERN apart into the decisions they hide.

kits.name: rag-blueprint
kits.description: Build and audit production retrieval systems on your own stack. Writes are single-threaded, the ADR is carried by a file, the role that writes the eval gate holds no shell to run it, and the red team refuses to run without a scratch target.

skills.name: rag-architecture
skills.line: Designs on the stack that is already there and names the failure modes: query condensation, chunking against the embedder's window, the retrieve-k to rerank-n cascade, filtered-recall cost, a cache keyed with entitlement, orphan chunks, and the dual-index migration a model change requires.

skills.name: rag-eval-suite
skills.line: Replaces the six-prompt vibe check with a gate that exits non-zero: a human-validated core that is the only part allowed to block, per-format metrics with a 30-pair floor, latency and cost, a recorded baseline, and faithfulness kept advisory.

skills.name: rag-threat-drills
skills.line: Runs injection, minimal-count poisoning, entitlement bypass cold and against a warm cache, cross-tenant probes, exfiltration and denial of wallet — against a scratch target only, each CONFIRMED, MITIGATED or NO-ORACLE with its reproduction and both denominators.

kits.name: starter-skills
kits.description: Three skills for the writing a repository asks for constantly — a commit message, a pull-request description, and release notes.

kits.name: test-integrity
kits.description: Find the tests that cannot fail. The oracle breaks the behaviour and watches whether the test notices; the only role that can write cannot run anything, so no stage verifies its own work.

skills.name: coverage-truth
skills.line: Report what a coverage number actually measures here, the exclusion list nobody reads, and which files are high-coverage and low-assurance.

skills.name: flake-hunt
skills.line: Find tests whose result depends on order, timing, seed or shared state, established across runs and with the mechanism named rather than called flaky.

skills.name: mutation-probe
skills.line: Prove whether a test can fail by breaking the behaviour it covers and watching whether it notices. PROVEN, BLIND or NO-ORACLE, never covered.

skills.name: vacuous-check
skills.line: Read tests for assertions that cannot fail and rank them for a mutation run, as suspicions with a path:line rather than verdicts.
